meaning: A message that pretends to be from a company you trust. It tries to get you to click a link and share private details.
clues: Someone is trying to get your private details or your money.
The sender pretends to be a company you know and trust, like your bank.
It comes as an email or text. It usually urges you to open a link or attachment, not to call a number.
The message often says there's a problem with your account and you must act fast.
Its name has eight letters and starts with P.

decoys.meaning: Someone says your computer has a problem. Then they ask for money or access to fix it.
Harmful software that scrambles your files. It demands payment to unscramble them.
Someone uses your name or account numbers without your permission, such as to buy things in your name.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Say a text claims there's a problem with your bank account and gives you a link. Try it: don't tap the link. Call the bank using a number you already know is real.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: When a caller said they were from the bank, we looked up the number in the phone book and called back. That habit still works.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Hurry-up words like 'act now' are a warning sign too.

sources.name: FTC, How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams
